name: Retinaldehyde (Retinal)

card.summary: The vitamin A form one step before retinoic acid, sold in OTC serums as a middle-ground retinoid; skin-specific human evidence is sparse and mostly old or still registered.
card.note: Do not confuse with the retina (eye anatomy), which dominates search results. Skin trials are few and small.

quick.overview:
Retinaldehyde (retinal) is the aldehyde form of vitamin A. In the body, it is part of the pathway that converts retinol into retinoic acid, the active form that tretinoin supplies directly [1]. It is also the light-sensing chromophore in vision, which is what most of the biological literature about it concerns [1].

In skincare it is sold as an over-the-counter retinoid positioned between retinol and prescription tretinoin. Published skin studies are few: an exploratory 1999 trial in rosacea, a 1999 human tolerance study, and a registered split-face study in aging skin [2][3][4].
quick.mechanism: Retinal is described as a precursor to retinoic acid, which acts through retinoic acid receptors (RARs) and retinoid X receptors to influence gene expression, cell differentiation and epithelial maintenance [1]. The 1999 rosacea trial described retinaldehyde as a retinoic acid precursor [2].
quick.risks: The 1999 trial of topical retinaldehyde in humans specifically assessed tolerance, but its results are not summarized in the source reviewed [3]. No published data in the sources reviewed quantify irritation or other adverse effects for retinaldehyde on skin. Retinal is chemically reactive and oxidizes readily, according to Grokipedia [1].

lead: Retinaldehyde, usually shortened to retinal, is the aldehyde form of vitamin A (retinol) with the formula C20H28O [1]. In biology it is best known as the chromophore of vertebrate vision, where its 11-cis isomer binds opsin proteins, and as an intermediate that can be converted onward to retinoic acid [1]. In cosmetic skincare, it is sold as a retinoid said to sit between retinol and tretinoin in strength.

Skin-focused evidence is thin. A 1999 exploratory clinical study applied a 0.05% retinaldehyde cream daily for 6 months to women with vascular signs of facial rosacea, and a companion 1999 randomized study examined its tolerance in humans [2][3]. A split-face study of stabilized retinaldehyde in aging skin (56 participants) is registered as completed [4].
In looksmaxxing forums, retinal appears as a lower-strength option that some users alternate with stronger prescription retinoids while skin adjusts [5].
infobox: Visual chromophore; intermediate between retinol and retinoic acid [1]

paras: Retinal has a beta-ionone ring joined to a polyene chain that ends in an aldehyde group; the all-trans and 11-cis geometric isomers are the biologically most relevant [1]. According to Grokipedia, the aldehyde group makes it reactive, prone to oxidation to retinoic acid and to forming Schiff bases with amines, which means it requires protection from air and light for storage [1].

In the eye, 11-cis-retinal photoisomerizes to all-trans-retinal to start the phototransduction cascade, and the visual cycle regenerates it [1]. Beyond vision, retinal is a precursor to retinoic acid, which regulates gene expression through retinoic acid and retinoid X receptors [1]. Most biomedical papers mentioning retinal concern the eye's retina and not skin.

Rosacea. A 1999 exploratory clinical and instrumental study tested a 0.05% retinaldehyde cream, applied once daily for 6 months, in female patients with persistent erythema and telangiectasia, prompted by anecdotal observations that retinoic acid may help mild rosacea [2].
Tolerance. A 1999 randomized clinical trial examined tolerance of topical retinaldehyde in humans [3].
Aging skin. A split-face study of stabilized retinaldehyde in skin aging and photoaging (56 participants, started 2023) is registered as completed on ClinicalTrials.gov [4].
No head-to-head trials of retinaldehyde against tretinoin or retinol for acne or photoaging were found in the sources reviewed.

On looksmax.org, one user asked whether to alternate leftover retinal with tazarotene each night while their skin adjusted to the prescription retinoid; a reply advised using only the tazarotene [5]. The thread also asks about obtaining prescription retinoids from overseas pharmacies [5]. The wiki does not reproduce application schedules.

timeline.event: Exploratory rosacea trial and a human tolerance trial of topical retinaldehyde published [2][3].
Split-face study of stabilized retinaldehyde in aging skin begins [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org retinal is mentioned occasionally as a gentler option to bridge toward stronger retinoids [5].

claims.claim: Retinal can be alternated with a prescription retinoid while skin adjusts
claims.believers: A poster describes planning to cycle leftover retinal with tazarotene each night during adjustment [5].
claims.experts: No published study in the sources reviewed tests alternating or combining retinaldehyde with tazarotene or tretinoin.

claims.claim: Retinal sits between retinol and tretinoin in strength
claims.believers: Described in product marketing and enthusiast discussion as a middle-ground retinoid.
claims.experts: Retinal is chemically one conversion step from retinoic acid [1]. The sources reviewed contain no comparative human trial against retinol or tretinoin.
